title: 5e-3: git-organizational biomarkers
description:
## Parent

sutra/83 (5e PRD: health metrics + similarity system)

## What to build

The three strongest defect predictors from the repowise calibration, all consuming the commit_files + commits tables from sutra/67:

- co_change_scatter (weight 1.80): count of distinct co-change partners per file over a configurable window. Fires when scatter >= 8 AND >= 3 commits in 90d.
- change_entropy (weight 1.51): Hassan's History Complexity Metric (ICSE 2009). Per-commit entropy contribution = log2(|F|), distributed 1/|F| per file, decay-weighted with tau=180d half-life. Drop commits wider than 30 files.
- ownership_risk (weight 1.38): Bird et al. FSE 2011. Fires when top owner share < 40% OR 3+ minor contributors (each < 5% of commits).

Plus: hidden_coupling (co-change >= 50% of shared commits with no static import edge), multi-agent ownership aliases via .sutra/owners.toml.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] health/git_metrics module with co_change_scatter, change_entropy, ownership_risk implementations
- [ ] All three consume commit_files + commits tables (no separate git log pass)
- [ ] hidden_coupling: files with >= 50% co-change correlation AND no static import edge, severity escalating at 65% and 80%
- [ ] .sutra/owners.toml parsing for multi-agent ownership aliases (agent authors → human dispatcher)
- [ ] Without owners.toml, agents treated as distinct contributors (conservative default)
- [ ] All biomarkers produce HealthFinding structs integrated into the parse pipeline
- [ ] Tests: each algorithm independently — partner counting, decay-weighted entropy computation, ownership threshold logic, alias resolution

## Blocked by

- sutra/84 (5e-1: health finding model)
- sutra/67 (commit_files + commits tables — must include committed_at and author columns)"
